problem: Panoramic-camera VLN models (ETPNav, GridMM) reach ~57% SR on R2R-CE but cannot be deployed on common monocular robots, while native monocular VLN agents stay below ~39% SR. Prior sim-to-real work relies on panoramic cameras or 2D laser scanners that miss obstacles at other heights and cannot recognise traversable landmarks such as doors and stairs.
motivation: Most real robots have only a narrow-FOV RGB-D camera (69° HFOV, 42° VFOV on RealSense D435), because panoramic RGB-D rigs are costly and bulky. The authors want to keep the high-performing panoramic VLN pipeline and instead give the monocular robot panoramic traversability and semantic perception, so the models transfer with little change.
key_idea: Replace panoramic observation with a monocular-RGB-D semantic traversable map for waypoint prediction plus pre-trained 3D feature fields (HNR) that render CLIP features of the unseen views, so panoramic VLN models run unchanged on a monocular robot.
insight: Simply zeroing the non-forward views of a panoramic model collapses performance (SR 56.1 → 32.9 on R2R-CE val-unseen), so panoramic perception is essential. Rendering novel views from the feature fields recovers 12 points of SR (44.9), and keeping the fields across episodes adds a little more (45.8). Removing the semantic map hurts most among the traversable-map components (SR 40.1 vs 44.9), showing that traversable landmarks such as doors and stairs matter. The cost is more exploration, which lowers SPL.
method: Global map ground-projection: monocular depth is projected into a 512×512 occupancy map (void/free/occupied, 5 cm per pixel), and a pre-trained UNet's segmentation into a 27-class semantic map, both accumulated during navigation.

Agent-centric refinement: 192×192 crops of both maps plus learnable positional embeddings (16 channels) go through two UNets that denoise the crops and fill in unobserved regions, trained with pixel-wise cross-entropy against ground-truth maps built from Matterport3D.

Traversable map prediction: another UNet takes the refined semantic, occupancy and positional channels (27+3+16) and outputs a traversability heatmap. It is trained with MSE against a mixture of Gaussians (σ=5) centred on the CWP ground-truth waypoints from the R2R connectivity graph.
Candidate waypoints: the heatmap is split into 12 sectors of 30°, the peak in each sector is taken, occupied cells are removed, and the Top-K are kept.

3D feature fields (HNR, pre-trained, not retrained): CLIP-ViT-B/16 features of the RGB frame are lifted to 3D using depth. Volume rendering gives an 8×8×512 feature map for each novel view, and a transformer decoder turns it into a 512-d view embedding aligned with CLIP.

Panorama synthesis and VLN policy: at each step the forward view uses real CLIP features and the other 11 of 12 views use predicted features. These feed the frozen-architecture panoramic VLN models (ETPNav topological map + graph transformer, or GridMM), fine-tuned on R2R-CE (10K episodes) and RxR-CE (20K episodes) and initialised from the baselines.
Deployment: a 360° rotation at step 1 initialises the maps and fields; the system runs on a LoCoBot WX250 with a laptop GTX 1060 under ROS Noetic.

setting.backbone: ETPNav / GridMM (fine-tuned) + HNR 3D feature fields with CLIP-ViT-B/16 (pre-trained, frozen) + UNet semantic/traversable map predictors (trained)
setting.training_data: Waypoint/map predictor: 20K random 15-step trajectories in Habitat (Matterport3D GT semantics, CWP waypoint annotations). VLN policy: R2R-CE 10K episodes / RxR-CE 20K episodes, initialised from trained ETPNav/GridMM. HNR used pre-trained without further training.
setting.observation: monocular RGB-D (forward-facing, 90° HFOV on R2R-CE, 79° on RxR-CE, RealSense 69°×42° in the real world)
setting.action_space: predicted navigable waypoints (Top-K from the traversable map) executed with low-level actions (forward 0.25 m, turn 15°)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT semantics/waypoints used only for training the map predictor)

results: On R2R-CE, ETPNav w/ Feature Fields with a monocular camera reaches 44.9 SR on val-unseen and 43.7 SR on test-unseen, over 7 points above the best previous monocular methods (WS-MGMap 38.9, NaVid 37.4 on val-unseen). On RxR-CE val-unseen it gets 25.5 SR vs NaVid's 23.8, but SPL is lower than NaVid's on both benchmarks. In the real world it reaches 42.0 SR vs 15.0 for WS-MGMap and 10.0 for CM².
limitations: The maps and feature fields depend on past observations, so the agent explores more before deciding; paths get longer and SPL is clearly lower (30.4 vs 49 for panoramic ETPNav).
A sizeable gap to true panoramic performance remains (44.9 vs 57 SR on R2R-CE val-unseen).
Real-world evaluation is small (100 samples, one lab environment, one robot), and the agent needs an initial 360° rotation.
